R258.note: Prefix startsWith replaced with exact Set.contains allowlist, closing the bypass; specific class names (cases.deserialization.SafeReport/ReportMetadata) are a plausible placeholder for the endpoint's report classes, openly noted as needing tailoring.

R259.note: Allowlist is the correct primary defence for dynamic require, but hardcodes only 3 plugin names with no evidence the real ./plugins directory contains exactly that set, risking rejection of other legitimate plugins; stated as the fix but not flagged as incomplete.

R260.note: Rebuilds the command as a proper RESP array with length-prefixed bulk strings, the correct fix for raw-socket Redis injection; all three fields (sessionId, agentNote, updatedAt) are preserved as data values.

R261.note: Replaces shell exec with Files.list(), the appropriate native API for directory listing, eliminating the shell entirely; signature and parameter usage unchanged.

R262.note: Drops sh -c in favor of direct exec.Command with an argument array, adds a host/IP allowlist regex, and inserts -- before the operand to close the residual flag-injection gap; output/response handling preserved.

R263.note: No Fix section or code is provided at all - only prose describing what a fix would do; the dynamic $renderer->$macro() dispatch is left completely unchanged and still exploitable.

R264.note: Same exact-match Set allowlist fix as R258; class names (com.example.report.Report/ReportData) plausibly match the domain implied by the original prefix check.

R265.note: Replaces default AES/ECB with AES/GCM using a fresh random 12-byte IV prepended to the ciphertext before Base64 encoding; still a Base64 string decryptable by the key holder, and the 400-on-missing-ssn behavior is unchanged.

R266.note: Correctly identifies that ProcessBuilder's argument array alone doesn't stop cmd.exe's re-parsing of a .bat target and adds a character allowlist, but the pattern disallows spaces/other characters a legitimate report name could contain; disclosed but not shown to match real report-name conventions.

R267.note: Switches to JNDI's parameterized search(filter, filterArgs, cons) API with {0} placeholder, which RFC-4515-escapes the value automatically; passing new SearchControls() correctly reproduces the null-controls default behavior of the original call.

R268.note: Drops shell=True for an argument list, closing the command injection; adds an os.path.basename() check against a different weakness (path traversal) that is unlikely to reject legitimate flat upload filenames, and is stated plainly.

R269.note: Adds RFC 4515 hex-escaping of \, *, (, ), and null before concatenation into the filter, the standard fix; does not otherwise restrict or alter accepted usernames.

R270.note: Replaces Process.Start/cmd.exe with .NET's native Ping class, eliminating the sink; the added hostname/IP allowlist regex excludes colons, which would reject legitimate IPv6 host values that the native Ping API otherwise supports.

R271.note: Extracts deleteInvoice into a separate @Service bean so the @PreAuthorize advice is applied through the Spring proxy on the batch-job call path, the standard fix for self-invocation bypass; no other behavior altered.

R272.note: Canonicalizes both the store directory and requested file and rejects any resolved path outside it (with a separator-suffixed prefix check to avoid partial-name false positives), the standard path-traversal fix; the added rejection is the fix itself, not an unrelated restriction.
